concerns.text: FR-010 defines the validation target as the proportion of total $R^{2}$ attributable to pairwise interaction terms, calculated by summing off‑diagonal SHAP interaction contributions and dividing by the model’s overall $R^{2}$. This target is derived from the same model whose performance it is meant to validate, creating a circular validation loop: the model must achieve a ≥ 70 % proportion of variance explained by interactions, but that proportion is computed from the model’s own SHAP values, not from an independent external measurement.

The metric in FR-010 (SHAP‑derived interaction contribution divided by $R^{2}$) is not a standard or theoretically justified measure of the variance explained by interactions. SHAP interaction values decompose model output, not variance, and there is no established relationship guaranteeing that the summed SHAP interaction magnitude corresponds to a proportion of $R^{2}$. Using this non‑standard metric as a hard success criterion lacks methodological validity.
